e.description: Semi-developed BLM campground and boat-ramp site with no drinking water or refuse containers. A toilet serves the colocated boat-ramp area.
e.name: Moonstone Campground and Boat Ramp

e.description: Five no-fee, non-reservable sites have picnic tables, fire rings, seasonal potable water and a vault toilet.
e.name: Pioneer Campground

e.description: Seven primitive, no-fee, non-reservable sites have a vault toilet; potable water is unavailable.
e.name: Five Points Campground

e.description: Ten non-reservable camping units include two double-family units. Picnic tables, fire rings, seasonal potable water and vault toilets are provided.
e.name: Bowns Campground

e.description: Ten first-come, nonelectric sites accept tents, RVs and trailers. Vault toilets are provided, but potable water is unavailable.
e.name: Easley Campground

e.description: This open, no-fee Forest Service camping area has vault toilets. Its official infrastructure record uses both Baker Creek Camping Area and Baker Creek Campground as names.
e.name: Baker Creek Camping Area

e.description: Twenty-eight nonelectric sites accept tents, RVs and trailers; 26 are reservable. Potable water and restrooms are not currently listed as available.
e.name: North Fork Campground

e.description: Thirty first-come sites include one double site; a separate reservable tent-only group area is also available. Flush toilets are provided, but potable water is unavailable.
e.name: Wood River Campground

e.description: Eleven first-come, nonelectric sites have a vault toilet but no potable water. The normal operating season is May through September.
e.name: Murdock Campground

e.description: Seven first-come, nonelectric sites have a vault toilet but no potable water. RVs and trailers are not recommended because turning around is difficult.
e.name: Caribou Campground

e.description: Dispersed camping area along the North Fork of the Big Wood River with no potable water and a 10-day stay limit.
e.name: Cougar Dispersed Camping Area

e.description: This nonelectric group campground accommodates up to 150 people and 75 vehicles. It is reservable as a group or first-come by individual site and has vault toilets, picnic tables and no potable water.
e.name: Chemeketan Campground

e.description: Twenty-seven public nonelectric sites accommodate tents, trailers and RVs; the official inventory also includes a management site. Vault toilets are provided, and there are no electric, water or sewer
e.name: Alturas Inlet Campground

e.description: All sites are first-come. Vault toilets are provided, but potable water is unavailable; maximum stay is 10 days within a 30-mile radius.
e.name: North Shore Campground

e.description: Eleven first-come units—eight single and three double—have vault toilets but no potable water. Maximum stay is 10 days within a 30-mile radius.
e.name: Smokey Bear Campground

e.description: Church recreation camp with cabins, a lodge kitchen, restrooms, showers and established fire rings. Only Church members may reserve; nonmembers may attend with members.
e.name: Smokey Lodge
e.operator: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints

e.description: Program and retreat camp using cabin lodging; hosted groups of 15-150 are accepted by advance reservation. Rustic cabins use a central shower house.
e.name: Luther Heights Bible Camp

e.description: Organized camp and retreat facility offering cabin lodging plus RV, trailer and tent space for selected programs. Advance registration is required; shower houses are available and pets are not permitt
e.name: Camp Perkins

e.description: Church recreation camp with cabins, a lodge kitchen, restrooms, showers, fire rings and a dumpster. Only Church members may reserve; nonmembers may attend with members.
e.name: Camp Cabin Creek
e.operator: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints

e.description: Twelve first-come campsites—nine single and three double—have vault toilets but no potable water. A day-use picnic area is adjacent.
e.name: Pettit Lake Campground
